extracted.intended_audience: Citizens and voters considering the structure of a federal government; readers interested in constitutional design and the stability of confederacies
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and summarizes normative criteria and historical lessons about the strengths and weaknesses of confederacies and federations — what features make unions stable or fragile. Useful for assessing constitutional design choices (powers, representation, enforcement, fiscal and military instruments, and sources of popular attachment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of national powers to commerce, finance, negotiation, and war
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce, finance, negotiation, and war seem to comprehend all the objects which have charms for minds governed by [ambition]; and all the powers necessary to those objects ought, in the first instance, to be lodged in the national depository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast national responsibilities with 'mere domestic police' matters which should remain with states; concentrate in national government only those powers necessary for general/global concerns to avoid unnecessary usurpation of state authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserve of local/domestic police to state governments
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation of the mere domestic police of a State appears to me to hold out slender allurements to ambition... The administration of private justice between the citizens of the same State, the supervision of agriculture and of other concerns of a similar nature... are proper to be provided for by local legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep immediate, personal, and locally sensitive matters (criminal and civil justice, agriculture, familiar concerns) under state/local control to preserve local attachment and to limit central ambition.

rubrics_metrics.name: State governments' superior influence over their people
rubrics_metrics.description: It will always be far more easy for the State governments to encroach upon the national authorities than for the national government to encroach upon the State authorities... the greater degree of influence which the State governments... will generally possess over the people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that proximity and administration of local affairs give state governments diffuse but powerful influence; constitutional design must account for this asymmetry of influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration of criminal and civil justice as prime source of popular attachment
rubrics_metrics.description: There is one transcendant advantage belonging to the province of the State governments... the ordinary administration of criminal and civil justice. This ... is the most powerful, most universal, and most attractive source of popular obedience and attachment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because courts and local justice regulate immediate life and property, they cement popular loyalty; whoever controls ordinary justice holds powerful grounds of influence — a design consideration for allocation of judicial authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distance/diffusiveness reduces popular affection for government
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a known fact in human nature, that its affections are commonly weak in proportion to the distance or diffusiveness of the object... the people of each State would be apt to feel a stronger bias towards their local governments than towards the government of the Union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The more remote or abstract national administration is from daily concerns, the less attachment it will inspire; central institutions should be structured to mitigate this natural tendency if national loyalty is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Many minute local interests create 'rivulets of influence' favoring local governments
rubrics_metrics.description: The variety of more minute interests, which will necessarily fall under the superintendence of the local administrations, and which will form so many rivulets of influence, running through every part of the society...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect local administrations to cultivate many small, distributed sources of influence across society; this multiplies the counterweight to national power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal constitutions possess inherent weakness and must be organized for force
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an inherent and intrinsic weakness in all federal constitutions; and that too much pains cannot be taken in their organization, to give them all the force which is compatible with the principles of liberty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge constitutional fragility and deliberately design institutions (powers, enforcement, fiscal base) to provide the necessary force without sacrificing liberty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk from concentration of strength into particular deposits (feudal analogy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The separate governments in a confederacy may aptly be compared with the feudal baronies... the points of similitude consist in the rivalship of power... and in the CONCENTRATION of large portions of the strength of the community into particular DEPOSITS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concentrated local power (like feudal barons) can rival or obstruct the national head; constitutional arrangements should avoid allowing concentrated local deposits of strength that can act as semi-sovereign rivals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative appointment method (deputies appointed wholly by member states) creates weakness and corruption
rubrics_metrics.description: The powers... were administered by deputies appointed wholly by the cities in their political capacities; and exercised over them in the same capacities. Hence the weakness, the disorders, and finally the destruction of the confederacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When federal delegates are instruments of member governments rather than representatives of the whole people, they can be corrupted or dominated by powerful members; design representative selection and accountability mechanisms to reduce this vulnerability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powerful members are likely to tyrannize over the weaker in confederacies
rubrics_metrics.description: The more powerful members, instead of being kept in awe and subordination, tyrannized successively over all the rest... deputies of the strongest cities awed and corrupted those of the weaker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without mechanisms to check dominant members, confederacies tend to domination by the strong; include balancing provisions to prevent sequential hegemony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of unanimity or near-unanimity cripples federal action
rubrics_metrics.description: In all important cases... unanimity and the sanction of their constituents are requisite... In all these cases, however, unanimity and the sanction of their constituents are requisite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision rules that demand unanimity make federal action slow, paralyzed, or impossible; pragmatic majority/qualified-majority rules better enable timely collective decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence of common fiscal and military instruments undermines union
rubrics_metrics.description: They have no common treasury; no common troops even in war; no common coin; no common judicatory; nor any other common mark of sovereignty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A functioning union typically needs a common treasury, common defence forces, common currency, and joint judicial mechanisms; lacking these, the union is fragile and subject to breakdown in crises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal coercion/enforcement is ineffective when members remain sovereign
rubrics_metrics.description: The diet is a representation of sovereigns and that the laws are addressed to sovereigns, renders the empire a nerveless body, incapable of regulating its own members... The impossibility of maintaining order and dispensing justice among these sovereign subjects...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laws addressed to sovereign political bodies without effective enforcement mechanisms are weak; the constitution must provide means to compel compliance or adjudicate disputes effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign powers exploit internal divisions of confederacies
rubrics_metrics.description: Philip... by his intrigues and bribes... made himself master of the confederacy... The Romans... seduced the members from the league... by representing to their pride the violation it committed on their sovereignty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fragmentation and rivalry invite foreign intervention; stronger central capacity and internal cohesion reduce vulnerability to external manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local pride, jealousy, and sovereign repellant quality resist consolidation/reform
rubrics_metrics.description: The repellant quality, incident to the nature of sovereignty, and which time continually strengthens, prevents any reform whatever, founded on a proper consolidation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate and design around entrenched local sovereignty and pride which will resist constitutional consolidation absent incentives or constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: An executive without territorial revenue or resources is materially weak
rubrics_metrics.description: In quality of emperor, he possesses no territory within the empire, nor receives any revenue for his support... But his revenue and dominions, in other qualities, constitute him one of the most powerful princes in Europe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An effective federal executive generally needs a stable revenue base and material resources; mere nominal prerogatives without means reduce practical authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lengthy deliberations among sovereign members impede timely military response
rubrics_metrics.description: Military preparations must be preceded by so many tedious discussions, arising from the jealousies, pride, separate views, and clashing pretensions of sovereign bodies, that before the diet can settle the arrangements, the enemy are in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defense requires decision-making speed and centralized command; federations requiring protracted consensus are at strategic disadvantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on religion, superstition, or oaths as enforcement is fragile
rubrics_metrics.description: The Amphictyons had in their hands the superstition of the times, one of the principal engines by which government was then maintained; they had a declared authority to use coercion... As a further provision... they took an oath mutually to defend and protect the united cities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noninstitutional bonds (religion, oaths) can temporarily support federal authority but are insufficient foundations for durable coercive power or compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common laws, customs, weights, measures, and coin foster effective union
rubrics_metrics.description: It appears that the cities had all the same laws and customs, the same weights and measures, and the same money... This circumstance alone proves a very material difference in the genius of the two systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal and economic uniformity across members increases compatibility and reduces friction; harmonization is a practical path to stronger union.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition, tenure, and appointment terms of federal representatives matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The States-General... consisting usually of about fifty deputies appointed by the provinces. They hold their seats, some for life, some for six, three, and one years; from two provinces they continue in appointment during pleasure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Who selects federal delegates, their term lengths, and stability of appointment affect federal action and susceptibility to provincial manipulation; design representative institutions for accountability to the union as a whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constituent restraints (provincial consent requirements) limit federal efficacy
rubrics_metrics.description: The provinces are restrained, unless with the general consent, from entering into foreign treaties; from establishing imposts injurious to others... In all these cases, however, unanimity and the sanction of their constituents are requisite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When constituent members retain veto-like controls over federal acts, the central authority is limited; consider necessary delegations of authority and appropriate decision rules to permit national action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudicatory mechanisms for disputes among members are essential
rubrics_metrics.description: They are subject in all cases to be judged by the emperor and diet, and in their private capacities by the aulic council and imperial chamber... The Swiss provision: parties choose four judges out of the neutral cantons, who... pronounce definitive sentence, which all the cantons are bound to enforce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective neutral tribunals and binding adjudication procedures are necessary to resolve internal disputes and prevent escalation; absent credible dispute resolution, leagues fracture.
